title: A Study of Performance Portability of Low-bit Fused Matrix-Vector Multiplication Kernels in SYCL
problem: Understanding performance portability of portable programming models (SYCL) vs vendor-specific models (CUDA, HIP) is critical for cross-platform adoption. Low-bit fused matrix-vector operations (GEMV) are increasingly important for AI/ML but lack SYCL evaluation and portability analysis.
motivation: SYCL promises performance portability across GPUs (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel). However, specific workloads (low-bit GEMV) reveal gaps. Understanding causes of performance differences enables better SYCL optimization and guides vendor implementations.
method: Implement low-bit fused GEMV kernels in CUDA, HIP, and SYCL. Evaluate performance across GPU types: datacenter (A100, MI100), desktop (RTX3090, MI250), laptop (RTX4050, MI28). Analyze performance gaps via profiling: loop unrolling, kernel dispatch overhead, sum reduction efficiency.
key_novelty: First systematic SYCL performance portability study for low-bit GEMV; identifies specific optimization barriers.
contributions: CUDA, HIP, SYCL implementations of low-bit fused GEMV
Performance evaluation across GPU tiers (datacenter, desktop, laptop)
Identification of SYCL optimization barriers (loop unrolling, dispatch, reduction)
Actionable insights for SYCL vendors and developers
hardware_target: NVIDIA GPUs (datacenter: A100; desktop: RTX3090; laptop: RTX4050)
AMD GPUs (datacenter: MI100/MI250; desktop: MI250; laptop: MI28)

metrics.focus: Performance gaps (SYCL vs CUDA/HIP), throughput, utilization
metrics.root_causes: Loop unrolling, kernel dispatch overhead, sum reduction

findings.kernel_dispatch: SYCL dispatch overhead larger than CUDA/HIP
findings.sum_reduction: Inefficient reduction in SYCL (vs vendor-specific optimizations)

limitations: Abstract only - no specific performance numbers, no proposed SYCL optimizations, limited kernel types (GEMV only)
